title: Claim-bearing source evidence authenticated by identity but not semantic content
root_cause: The F055/F056 verifier authenticated exact review/comment/reply identities but did not bind the actual Codex finding body and accepted owner-reply semantics from shared SHA/run-id substring presence.
failure_mechanism: An evidence verifier can validate object identity while leaving claim-bearing free-form content mutable or semantically interchangeable, allowing unrelated, swapped, or negating commentary to satisfy the evidence check.
violated_invariant: When free-form commentary is elevated into bounded canonical evidence, the claim-bearing content must be independently bound to governed immutable/update identity or semantically validated fail-closed; IDs and incidental tokens alone are insufficient.
trigger_conditions: A verifier consumes free-form review, comment, or reply text as evidence.
Multiple semantically distinct claims can share SHAs, run IDs, thread metadata, or other incidental tokens.
The verifier authenticates comment or thread identity separately from the exact claim-bearing body.
applicable_scope: future MimiSeek evidence adapters that elevate free-form commentary into bounded canonical evidence
non_applicable_scope: structured machine records whose complete claim semantics are already schema-bound and immutable

repository_search.notes: PR #21 fresh review showed that the original DFP-0001 search was too narrow. The accepted PR #20 authority/CI verifier is hardened, but F053/F054 fix-evidence and F058 fix-baseline verifiers still have the same identity-without-semantic-body-binding mechanism. Issue #22 is the durable closure boundary; this search must not return to COMPLETED until those instances are hardened and the generalized family search is repeated.

title: Checkout filesystem existence mistaken for tracked Git authority
root_cause: The repeat-prevention validator used Path.is_file() and filesystem globbing to accept declared guard/regression/search artifacts, so checkout-local files could satisfy a repository-authority claim.
failure_mechanism: A repository validator can accidentally elevate mutable checkout state such as .git metadata, untracked files, or tracked symlink targets into durable evidence when it checks filesystem existence instead of exact tracked Git file identity.
violated_invariant: A MimiSeek record that claims a durable repository guard, regression, discovered instance, or searched file scope must resolve to a tracked regular file in the authoritative Git working tree; checkout-only state and symlinks are not repository evidence.
trigger_conditions: A validator accepts repository-relative paths as durable evidence or prevention references.
Validation runs in a checkout containing .git metadata or possible untracked files.
Filesystem existence or globbing is used as a proxy for tracked Git identity.
applicable_scope: MimiSeek self-development registries and validators that elevate repository paths into durable authority
repository-search declarations used to close confirmed development defects
non_applicable_scope: runtime temporary paths that are explicitly non-authoritative and never recorded as repository evidence

repository_search.notes: The PR #21 validator was the current instance. Remediation resolves tracked regular files through the exact HEAD Git tree and negative regressions cover .git metadata, untracked files, staged-only files, tracked symlink escape, and equivalent searched-scope cases.

title: Cross-chat process duplicated across multiple canonical-looking documents
root_cause: PR #21 placed normative Development Repeat Prevention rules in both the BASE-designated DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL owner and a new document that independently claimed to define the same cross-chat process.
failure_mechanism: Duplicating mutable normative process rules across two canonical-looking documents creates ambiguous authority and allows the copies to drift even when both are initially consistent.
violated_invariant: One mutable cross-chat development fact has one canonical owner. Supporting documentation may explain or index that owner but must not independently define the same normative process.
trigger_conditions: A new documentation file introduces process rules already owned by an accepted canonical document.
Both documents use normative closure/retrieval/acceptance language for the same cross-chat workflow.
A supporting document claims to define a process whose owner is already assigned by accepted governance.
applicable_scope: new explanatory documents that overlap accepted canonical owners
non_applicable_scope: immutable evidence indexes and historical records that point to canonical process authority without redefining it

repository_search.notes: The overlapping normative copies introduced by PR #21 are consolidated by keeping DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL.md as the sole normative owner and converting DEVELOPMENT_REPEAT_PREVENTION.md into an explicitly non-authoritative explanatory/index document. The unit regression protects the ownership markers and absence of duplicated normative sections.

title: Unintended repository Contents write moves exact HEAD and invalidates evidence
root_cause: The development chat selected GitHub Contents write actions for operations whose intended effect was not a repository-file byte change, allowing the Contents API to move the exact review HEAD unnecessarily.
failure_mechanism: An unintended repository-content write can move an exact-review HEAD even when the intended operation is metadata, thread/ref housekeeping, or byte-identical replacement, invalidating exact-head CI/review evidence and causing unnecessary reruns.
violated_invariant: Repository content writes in the MimiSeek development workflow are consequence-bearing and may be used only when the intended operation is an actual repository-file byte change. Non-file operations use their dedicated non-content actions, and byte-identical replacement content must not be submitted through a Contents write.
trigger_conditions: The development chat is about to call a repository Contents create/update action.
The intended operation is not an actual repository-file byte change, including PR metadata/comment/thread or branch-ref movement.
The replacement bytes may be identical or the write may introduce unrelated temporary content while exact-head CI/review evidence exists or is being established.
applicable_scope: ChatGPT-driven MimiSeek repository development using GitHub connector write actions
exact-head acceptance workflows where any branch commit invalidates current evidence
non_applicable_scope: intentional repository byte changes whose resulting HEAD is expected to require fresh CI/review

repository_search.notes: This failure family originates outside repository runtime code. PR #21 recorded two byte-identical Contents writes (`e52c4287...`, `ee58bb51...`) and then a NEW_VARIANT unintended Contents write (`e9d033ad...`) used instead of branch-ref fast-forward. No repository-owned executable fence controls connector tool selection, so DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL remains the procedural prevention owner.

prevention.manual_only_reason: The consequence-bearing choice between GitHub connector Contents writes and dedicated non-content GitHub actions occurs outside repository code/CI. Until the external execution substrate exposes a machine-enforceable write-intent/no-op fence, repository CI cannot prevent the chat from invoking the wrong connector action; the canonical Development Protocol therefore carries the explicit pre-write rule.

title: Bounded follow-up accepted without durable recoverable locator
root_cause: The registry validator required BOUNDED_FOLLOW_UP to contain a non-empty follow_up_refs list but treated each element as arbitrary non-empty text.
failure_mechanism: Unresolved process debt can appear durably bounded while its follow-up pointer is not independently recoverable, allowing free-form promises such as 'done later' to satisfy CI without a stable issue or repository artifact.
violated_invariant: Every bounded follow-up must identify durable recoverable work through a supported locator: an exact MimiSeek issue URL or a tracked regular file in the exact HEAD tree.
trigger_conditions: A machine record represents intentionally unresolved development work.
Closure depends on follow_up_refs surviving chat boundaries.
The validator checks only presence/non-emptiness rather than durable locator authority.
applicable_scope: future MimiSeek registries that represent unresolved repository-development debt
non_applicable_scope: purely explanatory prose that is not used to satisfy a machine closure state

repository_search.notes: PR #21 current-head review found the only current machine acceptance path for follow_up_refs. Remediation restricts each follow-up to a canonical MimiSeek issue URL or tracked regular exact-HEAD file and adds malformed/foreign/free-form negative regressions plus a tracked-file positive case.

title: Unknown repeat analysis can appear completed and disappear from startup view
root_cause: The validator accepted UNKNOWN_PENDING_ANALYSIS independently from repository_search status, while the active summary omitted unresolved repeat-analysis occurrences.
failure_mechanism: A repeat can remain causally unresolved while the same pattern advertises COMPLETED search with no follow-up and the development-start retrieval output hides the pending analysis, allowing unresolved prevention failure to vanish across chats.
violated_invariant: UNKNOWN_PENDING_ANALYSIS is explicitly temporary fail-closed state: any such REPEAT must keep the pattern in BOUNDED_FOLLOW_UP with durable follow-up and must be surfaced by active-pattern retrieval until reclassified.
trigger_conditions: Repository search state can independently be marked COMPLETED.
Startup retrieval summarizes patterns without exposing unresolved occurrence analysis.
non_applicable_scope: REPEAT occurrences whose prevention failure reason is already concretely classified

repository_search.notes: PR #21 current-head review found the cross-field gap in the repeat-prevention validator and startup summary. Remediation makes UNKNOWN_PENDING_ANALYSIS incompatible with COMPLETED and exposes pending occurrence IDs through --list-active.
